title: Optimizing Prompts for Text-to-Image Generation
finding: Promptist: an LM is supervised-fine-tuned on manually engineered prompts, then RL-tuned with a reward for aesthetics plus preserved user intent; on Stable Diffusion it beats manual prompt engineering on automatic metrics and human preference, and RL helps most on out-of-domain prompts (per authors).
why_for_us: Proof that a small rewriter tuned to ONE generator's preferred prompt style beats hand-written prompts; the gain is model-specific, so a rewriter for LTX-2.5 must be tuned/evaluated against LTX-2.5 outputs, not borrowed from SD.

title: Improving Text-to-Image Consistency via Automatic Prompt Optimization
finding: OPT2I: an LLM iteratively proposes revised prompts to maximize a prompt-image consistency score (DSG); boosts initial consistency by up to 24.9% DSG on MSCOCO/PartiPrompts while preserving FID (per authors).
why_for_us: Training-free recipe we can run today: LLM rewrites the shot prompt, render a cheap keyframe, score with a question-based checker (DSG-style 'is there X, is X doing Y'), keep the best prompt before spending video renders.

title: The Devil is in the Prompts: Retrieval-Augmented Prompt Optimization for Text-To-Video Generation
finding: RAPO: two branches - retrieval of modifiers from a relation graph plus a fine-tuned LLM that reformats prompts to the training-prompt distribution, and an instruction-following LLM rewrite - then picks the better prompt; improves static and dynamic quality dimensions of T2V output (per authors).
why_for_us: Key idea for open video models: rewrite user/Polish shot descriptions into the length, vocabulary and sentence structure of the model's training captions (for LTX: long, detailed English captions), and keep two rewrite variants per shot instead of one.

title: RAPO++: Cross-Stage Prompt Optimization for Text-to-Video Generation via Data Alignment and Test-Time Scaling
finding: Adds a closed-loop sample-specific stage that iteratively refines prompts using multi-source feedback (semantic alignment, spatial fidelity, temporal coherence, optical flow) and then distils the optimized prompt pairs back into the rewriter LLM; reports gains across five T2V models and five benchmarks without touching the generator (per authors).
why_for_us: Template for our loop: log (shot prompt, rewritten prompt, gate score) triples from batch runs, and after enough accepted shots fine-tune a small local rewriter on the winners so later shots need fewer retries.

title: PromptEnhancer: A Simple Approach to Enhance Text-to-Image Models via Chain-of-Thought Prompt Rewriting
finding: Decouples rewriter from generator: a chain-of-thought rewriter is RL-trained against an AlignEvaluator reward model built on a taxonomy of 24 T2I failure points; significantly improves image-text alignment on HunyuanImage 2.1 without changing its weights (per authors).
why_for_us: Their 24-point failure taxonomy is a ready checklist for our acceptance gate and keyframe critic (attribute binding, negation, counts, relations); the 'prompt enhancer shipped with an open model' pattern is what we should replicate for LTX keyframes.

title: Prompt-A-Video: Prompt your Video Diffusion Model via Preference-Aligned LLM
finding: Builds a video-model-specific prompt rewriter: reward-guided prompt evolution creates an optimal prompt pool for SFT of the LLM, then multi-dimensional video rewards produce pairs for DPO; effective across several video generation models (per authors).
why_for_us: Argues generic LLM rewriting is 'model-unaware'; a cheap path for us is SFT+DPO of a small LLM (LoRA, one GPU) on prompts ranked by our own acceptance gate on LTX-2.5 renders.

title: POS: A Prompts Optimization Suite for Augmenting Text-to-Video Generation
finding: Observes that for the same text, different noises give videos differing strongly in frame quality and temporal consistency, and that LLM prompt rewriting often causes semantic deviation; proposes an optimal-noise approximator (retrieve and invert a related video) plus a semantic-preserving rewriter, improving T2V models on benchmarks (per authors).
why_for_us: Two warnings for us: seed choice matters as much as prompt, and LLM rewrites can drift from the script - add a semantic-equivalence check (original vs rewritten shot description) before rendering.

title: VideoDirectorGPT: Consistent Multi-scene Video Generation via LLM-Guided Planning
finding: GPT-4 expands one prompt into a 'video plan' (scene descriptions, entities with layouts, backgrounds, consistency groupings of entities) that drives a layout-controlled generator; improves layout and movement control and multi-scene consistency while staying competitive on single-scene T2V (per authors).
why_for_us: Adopt the 'video plan' JSON as our shot list format: per shot entities, background, and explicit consistency groups (same speaker, same room) that map to shared reference keyframes/seeds.

title: DreamFactory: Pioneering Multi-Scene Long Video Generation with a Multi-Agent Framework
finding: Multi-agent LLM framework with a Key Frames Iteration Design Method for consistency and style across long videos; proposes Cross-Scene Face Distance Score and Cross-Scene Style Consistency Score and a dataset of over 150 human-rated multi-scene videos (per authors).
why_for_us: Cross-scene face distance is a metric we can implement directly in the gate (face embedding distance of the presenter vs the reference keyframe) to auto-reject identity drift between Polish talking-head shots.

title: FilmAgent: A Multi-Agent Framework for End-to-End Film Automation in Virtual 3D Spaces
finding: Director, screenwriter, actor and cinematographer agents iterate with feedback and revisions on scripts and camera setups; human evaluation over 15 ideas gives 3.98/5 average, beating baselines, and the GPT-4o multi-agent system surpasses single-agent o1 (per authors).
why_for_us: Evidence that role-split critique of the SCRIPT/shot plan (before rendering) pays off; cheap for us because it costs LLM tokens, not GPU minutes. Note results are in 3D virtual spaces, not diffusion video.

title: VideoGen-of-Thought: Step-by-step generating multi-shot video with minimal manual intervention
finding: Training-free pipeline: shot drafts expanded into five-domain specifications with self-validation, identity-preserving portrait tokens for cross-shot identity, and boundary-aware latent transitions; beats baselines by 20.4% in within-shot face consistency and 17.4% in style consistency with 10x fewer manual adjustments (per authors).
why_for_us: Most concrete numbers for multi-shot consistency vs single-pass; the five spec domains (character, background continuity, relationships, camera, lighting) are a good template for our per-shot prompt fields.

title: MAViS: A Multi-Agent Framework for Long-Sequence Video Storytelling
finding: Agents for script, shot design, character modeling, keyframes, animation and audio each follow an Explore-Examine-Enhance loop; Script Writing Guidelines adapt scripts to the capabilities of current generators; reports state-of-the-art assistive capability, visual quality and expressiveness (per authors).
why_for_us: Their 'write the script for what the generator can do' guideline matches our need: constrain shot descriptions to motions LTX-2.5 renders reliably (static camera, single speaker, short actions) instead of correcting afterwards.

title: AniMaker: Multi-Agent Animated Storytelling with MCTS-Driven Clip Generation
finding: Director, Photography, Reviewer and Post-Production agents; MCTS-Gen explores the multi-candidate clip space efficiently and AniEval judges each clip in context of neighbouring clips; notes a single low-quality clip can degrade the whole animation, and reports better VBench/AniEval scores with more efficient multi-candidate generation (per authors).
why_for_us: Closest analogue to our batch: several candidates per shot, reviewer agent, selection in context of adjacent shots. Suggests spending extra seeds adaptively on shots whose first candidates score low instead of a fixed N per shot.

title: Idea2Img: Iterative Self-Refinement with GPT-4V(ision) for Automatic Image Design and Generation
finding: GPT-4V cyclically revises T2I prompts, generates drafts, gives directional feedback and keeps a memory of the probed model's characteristics; a user preference study supports better semantic and visual quality than vanilla T2I (per authors).
why_for_us: Keep a persistent 'model memory' of what LTX-2.5 gets wrong (from gate logs) and feed it to the prompt-writing LLM, so retries are informed rather than blind reseeding.

title: Self-Correcting LLM-Controlled Diffusion Models
finding: SLD generates an image, assesses alignment with the prompt, and applies LLM-planned corrections in a closed loop; training-free, works with API models such as DALL-E 3, and rectifies a majority of incorrect generations in numeracy, attribute binding and spatial relations (per authors).
why_for_us: For keyframes (image stage before animation) fix-by-editing is cheaper than re-rendering: detect the error, inpaint/edit the keyframe, then animate - errors fixed at keyframe level do not cost video GPU time.

title: GenArtist: Multimodal LLM as an Agent for Unified Image Generation and Editing
finding: An MLLM agent decomposes complex requests into a tree of generation, editing and self-correction steps with step-by-step verification, selecting tools from a library; reports state-of-the-art results surpassing SDXL and DALL-E 3 (per authors).
why_for_us: Pattern for our keyframe stage: planner + tool library (ComfyUI workflows for generate / inpaint / face-fix / upscale) + verification after each step.

title: Maestro: Self-Improving Text-to-Image Generation via Agent Orchestration
finding: MLLM critic agents identify image weaknesses and give interpretable edit signals merged by a verifier agent; MLLM-as-judge pairwise comparisons discard problematic images and evolve prompts; improvement scales with stronger MLLM components (per authors).
why_for_us: Use pairwise comparison (candidate A vs B for the same shot) rather than absolute scores for ranking seeds; gains depend on judge strength, so a weak local VLM judge may cap the benefit.

title: Iterative Refinement Improves Compositional Image Generation
finding: A VLM critic guides step-by-step refinement of generations; versus compute-matched parallel sampling it gains 16.9% all-correct on ConceptMix (k=7), 13.8% on T2I-CompBench 3D-Spatial and 12.5% on Visual Jenga, with humans preferring it 58.7% vs 41.3% (per authors).
why_for_us: Direct evidence that, at equal compute, sequential critic-guided correction beats plain best-of-N for complex multi-constraint shots; simple shots probably still favour best-of-N.

title: Self-Correcting Text-to-Video Generation with Misalignment Detection and Localized Refinement
finding: VideoRepair: MLLM with auto-generated evaluation questions detects misaligned regions, preserves correct entities, and regenerates only problematic regions; training-free and model-agnostic, with substantial alignment gains on EvalCrafter and T2V-CompBench across four T2V backbones (per authors).
why_for_us: Video-level analogue of question-based checking: generate yes/no questions from the shot spec, ask a VLM on sampled frames, and if one entity fails, repair locally rather than discard the whole clip.

title: MJ-Bench: Is Your Multimodal Reward Model Really a Good Judge for Text-to-Image Generation?
finding: Benchmarks CLIP-style scorers, open VLMs and closed VLMs as judges: closed VLMs give better feedback on average (GPT-4o best); small scoring models beat open VLMs on text-image alignment and image quality, while VLMs are better on safety and bias; VLM judges are more accurate and stable with Likert-style natural-language scales than numeric ones (per authors).
why_for_us: Calibration guidance for our gate: do not trust an open VLM alone for quality/alignment auto-reject; combine small dedicated scorers for quality with a VLM for semantic checks, and ask the VLM for Likert labels, not 0-100 numbers.

title: Omni-Judge: Can Omni-LLMs Serve as Human-Aligned Judges for Text-Conditioned Audio-Video Generation?
finding: Across nine metrics, omni-LLM judges reach correlation with humans comparable to traditional metrics and excel on semantic alignment and audio-video-text coherence, but underperform on high-FPS perceptual metrics such as video quality and audio-video synchronization due to limited temporal resolution (per authors).
why_for_us: Critical for talking heads: do NOT rely on an LLM/VLM judge for lip-sync; keep a dedicated sync metric (SyncNet-style) in the gate and use the VLM only for semantic checks.

title: Scaling Inference Time Compute for Diffusion Models
finding: Gains from more denoising steps flatten after a few dozen; framing inference-time scaling as a search over noises with verifiers and search algorithms gives substantial quality improvements, and the best verifier/algorithm combination depends on the application (per authors).
why_for_us: Theoretical backing for our 'several seeds per shot + gate': spend compute on more seeds/search rather than more steps, and choose the verifier to match what we actually reject for (identity, lips, artifacts).

title: Video-T1: Test-Time Scaling for Video Generation
finding: Treats video test-time scaling as search over noise trajectories with verifiers; linear search over more noise candidates, and a cheaper Tree-of-Frames that expands and prunes branches autoregressively; more test-time compute consistently improves video quality (per authors).
why_for_us: Supports early pruning: evaluate candidates on partial/low-step previews and only finish the promising seeds; in ComfyUI this means a cheap preview pass before full-quality renders.

title: Test-Time Scaling of Diffusion Models via Noise Trajectory Search
finding: More denoising steps give quickly diminishing returns; MCTS over noise trajectories is meaningful but impractical, so an epsilon-greedy bandit search (explore at extreme timesteps, exploit at intermediate) works with non-differentiable rewards and exceeds baselines by up to 164% while matching MCTS (per authors).
why_for_us: Works with any black-box reward (our gate score); a future option once plain best-of-N saturates, but needs sampler-level hooks in ComfyUI.

title: ScalingNoise: Scaling Inference-Time Search for Generating Infinite Videos
finding: Most VDM use is a single generation attempt; ScalingNoise does one-step denoising of candidate noises into a preview clip, scores it with a reward anchored on previously generated content, and samples from a tilted noise distribution, improving long-video consistency (per authors).
why_for_us: One-step previews to rank seeds are a cheap filter we can test on the 5090: render N one-step previews, keep the top-k seeds for full renders, anchoring the score to the reference keyframe.

title: ROC-n-reroll: How verifier imperfection affects test-time scaling
finding: Proves Best-of-N and rejection sampling accuracy is governed by the verifier's ROC curve; rejection sampling beats BoN at fixed compute, both converge at infinite compute to a level set by the ROC slope near the origin, and rejection-sampling performance cannot be extrapolated from low compute (per authors; experiments on GSM8K).
why_for_us: Rendering more seeds only helps as far as the gate's ROC allows: measure the gate's false-accept rate on human-reviewed clips before increasing N; a noisy gate caps success no matter how many seeds.

title: Improving Video Generation with Human Feedback
finding: Large multi-dimensional pairwise preference dataset, VideoReward model that significantly outperforms existing reward models, and alignment for flow models: Flow-DPO beats Flow-RWR and SFT, while inference-time Flow-NRG applies reward guidance to noisy videos with user-weighted objectives (per authors).
why_for_us: VideoReward is a candidate off-the-shelf scorer for the gate; Flow-DPO is relevant since LTX is flow-based; Flow-NRG offers improvement without training.

title: VideoDPO: Omni-Preference Alignment for Video Diffusion Generation
finding: Adapts DPO to video diffusion with an OmniScore combining visual quality and text-video alignment, collects preference pairs automatically, and finds re-weighting pairs by score significantly affects alignment; substantial gains on both dimensions (per authors).
why_for_us: Our accepted vs rejected seeds per shot are free preference pairs; a LoRA-DPO on LTX-2.5 using gate scores is a plausible later step on one GPU.

title: Video Diffusion Alignment via Reward Gradients
finding: VADER backpropagates dense gradients from pre-trained reward models into video diffusion models, which is far more efficient in reward queries and compute than gradient-free approaches across several reward and video models (per authors).
why_for_us: If we fine-tune at all, reward-gradient LoRA is the most sample-efficient route, but backprop through video decoding is memory-heavy on 32GB; treat as experiment, not production.

title: DenseDPO: Fine-Grained Temporal Preference Optimization for Video Diffusion Models
finding: Whole-clip preference labels bias annotators toward low-motion clips; segment-level preferences on aligned pairs improve motion with one-third of the labeled data, and GPT predicts segment-level preferences about as well as fine-tuned video reward models (per authors).
why_for_us: Warning for our human review and gate: both may favour static, artifact-free clips over natural motion; label at segment level and watch for 'frozen presenter' bias.

title: Is It AI or Is It Me? Understanding Users’ Prompt Journey with Text-to-Image Generative AI Tools
finding: Interviews with 19 users describe structures and processes for writing, evaluating and refining prompts; users must overcome barriers in aligning AI to intent and in mastering prompt-crafting knowledge (per authors).
why_for_us: Supports shipping prompt templates and a shared library of known-good shot prompts to the reviewers, instead of each person re-learning LTX prompting.

title: Evolving Roles and Workflows of Creative Practitioners in the Age of Generative AI
finding: Interviews, videos and surveys of practitioners reflecting on GenAI projects yield factors describing perceived roles, challenges, benefits and interaction patterns across project stages (per authors).
why_for_us: Frame for defining the human reviewer's role per stage (script approval, keyframe approval, final clip) rather than only at the end.

title: The Prompt Artists
finding: Prolific T2I users develop prompt templates with slots, seek specialized vocabulary for distinctive outputs, and exploit model 'glitches' as styles (per authors).
why_for_us: Validates a template-with-slots approach for our shot prompts (presenter, setting, action, camera), maintained as versioned assets.

title: Digital "Double Hatters": Augmenting Audiovisual Creative Work with a Generative Text-to-Video Workflow
finding: Mixed-methods study (n=12) of freelance audiovisual professionals using a text-to-video probe: found easy to use, expressive and supporting many professional use cases, expanding their range into adjacent domains (per authors).
why_for_us: Small-sample evidence that professionals accept T2V workflows when they stay in control of structure; keep editorial decisions human, automate rendering.

title: Human Learning by Model Feedback: The Dynamics of Iterative Prompting with Midjourney
finding: Prompts predictably converge toward specific traits over iterations, partly because users notice missing details and partly by adapting to the model's preferred language style; this makes user data biased toward one model's preferences (per authors).
why_for_us: If we later train a rewriter on our own accepted prompts, expect it to encode LTX-2.5-specific style; re-collect when switching models.
